en: Dhammasaṅgaṇī 2:
Exposition 2.1 Section on the Arising of Consciousness (Cittuppādakaṇḍa)
2.1.5. Supramundane Wholesome States (Lokuttara-kusala) 2.1.5.1.
The Pure Path (Suddhika-paṭipadā) Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops supramundane jhāna that is leading to liberation, conducive to the waning of existence, for the abandoning of views,
and for the attainment of the first stage— secluded from sensual pleasures... [as before] ...entering and dwelling in the first jhāna,
which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge— at that time there is contact, there is feeling, there is perception.
There is volition, there is consciousness, there is applied thought, there is sustained thought, there is rapture, there is pleasure,
there is one-pointedness of mind; there is the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of mind,
the faculty of mental joy, the faculty of vital energy, and the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown."
There is right view, there is right intention, there is right speech, there is right action, there is right livelihood, there is right effort,
there is right mindfulness, there is right concentration; there is the power of faith, there is the power of energy,
there is the power of mindfulness, there is the power of concentration, there is the power of wisdom, there is the power of moral shame, and there is the power of moral dread.
There is non-greed, there is non-hatred, there is non-delusion; there is non-covetousness, there is non-ill will, there is right view;
there is moral shame, there is moral dread; there is tranquility of body, there is tranquility of mind;
there is buoyancy of body, there is buoyancy of mind; there is plasticity of body, there is plasticity of mind; there is wieldiness of body, there is wieldiness of mind.
There is lightness of body, lightness of mind, proficiency of body, proficiency of mind, rectitude of body,
rectitude of mind, mindfulness, clear comprehension, serenity, insight, exertion, and non-distraction; or whatever other conditioned,
immaterial phenomena exist at that time which have arisen dependently.
These states are wholesome.
What, at that time, is contact?
That which at that time is contact, the act of contacting, the state of contacting, the quality of having contacted.
This, at that time, is contact.
What, at that time, is feeling?

That which, at that time, is born of the contact of the mind-consciousness element corresponding to that [object], the mental gratification, the mental pleasure, the pleasant and happy experience born of mind-contact, the pleasant and happy feeling born of mind-contact—this is feeling at that time.
This, at that time, is feeling.
What, at that time, is perception?
That which, at that time, is born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element—perception, perceiving, the state of having perceived.
This, at that time, is perception.
What, at that time, is volition?
That which, at that time, is volition born of contact with the corresponding mind-consciousness element; the state of intending, the act of intending, the quality of having intended.
At that time, this is volition.
What at that time is consciousness?

That which at that time is consciousness, mind, mentation, heart, lucidity, the mind, the mind-base, the mind-faculty, cognition, the aggregate of cognition, and the corresponding element of mind-consciousness.
This is the state of mind at that time.
What is the applied thought (vitakka) at that time?
It is that which at that time is reasoning, applied thought, intention, absorption, close application, the directing of the mind, right intention, a factor of the path, and included within the path.
This, at that time, is applied thought (*vitakka*).
What, at that time, is sustained thought (*vicāra*)?
That which, at that time, is wandering, sustained thought, repeated sustained thought, mental preoccupation, the continuous threading of the mind, and the close examination [of the object].
At that time, this is what constitutes sustained application (*vicāra*).
What at that time is rapture (*pīti*)?
That which at that time is rapture, gladness, rejoicing, exultation, laughter, mirth, elation, buoyancy, mental satisfaction, and the factor of enlightenment that is rapture (*pītisambojjhaṅga*).
This, at that time, is rapture (pīti).
What, at that time, is pleasure (sukha)?

That which, at that time, is mental well-being, mental pleasure, a pleasant and pleasurable feeling born of mental contact, a pleasant and pleasurable sensation born of mental contact—this, at that time, is pleasure.
At that time, this is what constitutes happiness.
What at that time is one-pointedness of mind?
It is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-wavering, non-distraction, and state of mental non-distraction of the mind at that time.

Tranquillity, the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration, the factor of enlightenment that is concentration, the path factor, and that which is included within the path—
this, at that time, is one-pointedness of mind.
What, at that time, is the faculty of faith?
Whatever at that time is faith, being faithful, conviction, serene confidence, faith, the faculty of faith,
and the power of faith— this, at that time,
is the faculty of faith. What, at that time, is the faculty of energy?
Whatever at that time is the arousal of mental energy, exertion, striving, endeavor, effort, perseverance, fortitude, steadfastness,
unfaltering persistence, non-abandonment of desire, non-abandonment of the burden, the taking up of the burden,

energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, the path factor, and that which is included within the path— this is called the enlightenment factor of energy.
This, at that time, is the faculty of energy.
What, at that time, is the faculty of mindfulness?

That which, at that time, is mindfulness, constant mindfulness, specific mindfulness, mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not forgetting, the state of not losing hold, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness, the factor of enlightenment consisting of mindfulness, the path constituent, and that which is included within the path.
This, at that time, is the faculty of mindfulness.
What, at that time, is the faculty of concentration?
It is that which, at that time, is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-dispersal, non-distraction, and state of mental non-distraction of the mind.

Tranquility— the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration, the factor of enlightenment that is concentration, the path-factor, and that which is included within the path—
this at that time is the faculty of concentration.
What at that time is the faculty of wisdom?
Whatever at that time is wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, close discernment, precise discernment, sagacity, skill,
subtlety, discrimination, reflection, examination, breadth, intelligence, guidance, insight,
clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom; this is called the faculty of wisdom.
The palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena, right view,
the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment, a path-factor, included within the path— at that time,
this is what constitutes the faculty of wisdom.
What on that occasion is the faculty of mind (manindriya)?

That which on that occasion is thought (citta), mind (mano), mentation (mānasa), heart (hadaya), lucidity (paṇḍara), mind, the mind-base (manāyatana), the faculty of mind, consciousness (viññāṇa), the aggregate of consciousness, and the element of mind-consciousness born thereof—
this on that occasion is the faculty of mind.
What on that occasion is the faculty of mental joy (*somanassindriya*)?
That which on that occasion is mental well-being, mental pleasure, a pleasant and happy feeling born of mind-contact, a pleasant and happy sensation born of mind-contact—
this on that occasion is the faculty of mental joy.
What at that time is the life-faculty?
That which, for those immaterial phenomena, is the life-span, the persistence, the subsistence, the maintenance, the going-on, the occurrence,
the preservation, the life, the life-faculty— this at that time is the life-faculty.
What on that occasion is the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown"?

It is the wisdom, the understanding, the investigation, the thorough investigation, the investigation of phenomena, the discernment, the close examination, the close scrutiny, the close inspection, regarding those states that have not been known, not seen, not reached, not realized, and not directly experienced, for the purpose of realizing them.
Wisdom, skill, proficiency, discernment, reflection, investigation, vast intelligence, sagacity, guidance, insight, clear comprehension,

the goad, understanding, the faculty of understanding, the power of understanding, the sword of understanding, the palace of understanding, the light of understanding, the radiance of understanding, the lamp of understanding,
the jewel of understanding, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena, right view, and the factor of enlightenment that is the investigation of phenomena.
The path factor included in the path—
this, at that time, is the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown.
What, at that time, is right view?
Whatever at that time is wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, close discernment, precise discernment, sagacity, skill,
subtlety, discrimination, reflection, examination, breadth, intelligence, guidance, insight,
clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom; this is called the faculty of wisdom.
The palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom; non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view,
the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a factor of the path, included within the path— at that time,
this is what constitutes right view.
What on that occasion is right intention?
That which on that occasion is reasoning, thought, intention, application, mental application, the directing of the mind, right intention, a factor of the path, included within the path—
this on that occasion is right intention.
What at that time is right speech?

Whatever at that time is the refraining, abstaining, desisting, abstinence from, non-doing, non-committing, non-transgression of, not overstepping the limit of, and destruction of the bridge regarding the four types of verbal misconduct;
right speech as a factor of the path, included within the path—at that time, this is right speech.
What on that occasion is right action?

Whatever on that occasion is the desisting from the three kinds of bodily misconduct, the abstaining, the refraining, the abstinence, the non-doing, the non-performing, the non-transgression, the not overstepping the limit, the destruction of the bridge [of evil], which is right action, a factor of the Path,
included within the Path— this on that occasion is right action.
What on that occasion is right livelihood?

That which on that occasion is the refraining from, the abstaining from, the desisting from, the abstinence from, the non-performance, the non-doing, the non-transgression of, the not overstepping the limit of, the destruction of the bridge to wrong livelihood; this on that occasion is right livelihood, a factor of the path, included within the path.
This on that occasion is right livelihood.
What on that occasion is right effort?
It is, on that occasion, the arousal of mental energy, the striving, the exertion, the endeavor, the effort, the zeal,

the perseverance, the fortitude, the steadfastness, the state of unfaltering perseverance, the state of not laying down the burden, the state of not laying down the yoke, the sustained application of the burden.
Energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, the path factor, and that which is included within the path—
this, at that time, is right effort.
What, at that time, is right mindfulness?

Whatever at that time is mindfulness, recollection, constant mindfulness, mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not losing, the state of not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness, the factor of enlightenment that is mindfulness, the path-factor, and that which is included within the path—
this, at that time, is right mindfulness. What, at that time, is right concentration?
Whatever at that time is the stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-diffusion, non-distraction, state of mental non-dispersal, serenity, the faculty of concentration,
the power of concentration, right concentration, the concentration factor of enlightenment, the path factor,
and that which is included within the path— this, at that time, is right concentration.
What on that occasion is the power of faith?
Whatever on that occasion is faith, being faithful, conviction, serene confidence, faith, the faculty of faith, the power of faith—
this on that occasion is the power of faith.
What on that occasion is the power of energy?
It is the arousal of mental energy on that occasion, the striving, the exertion, the endeavor, the effort, the zeal,

the perseverance, the fortitude, the steadfastness, the state of unfaltering exertion, the state of not relinquishing desire, the state of not relinquishing the burden, and the sustained application of the burden.
Energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, the path factor, and that which is included within the path—
this, at that time, is the power of energy.
What, at that time, is the power of mindfulness?

Whatever at that time is mindfulness, recollection, constant mindfulness, mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not wobbling, the state of not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness, the factor of enlightenment consisting of mindfulness, the path-factor, and that which is included in the path—
this, at that time, is the power of mindfulness. What, at that time, is the power of concentration?
Whatever at that time is stability of the mind, steadfastness, stability, non-distraction, unperturbed state of mind, serenity, the faculty of concentration,
the power of concentration, right concentration, the factor of enlightenment that is concentration, the path-factor, and that which is included within the path—
this at that time is the power of concentration.
What on that occasion is the power of wisdom (paññābala)?

It is the wisdom on that occasion which is understanding, investigation, close investigation, thorough investigation of phenomena, discernment, discrimination, differentiation, erudition, proficiency,

subtlety, sagacity, reflection, examination, breadth, intelligence, clarity, insight, leading, light, radiance, truth, science, art, skill, resourcefulness, grasp, readiness, alertness, quickness, promptitude, depth, perspicuity, wisdom, the aggregate of wisdom, the absence of dullness, right view— this on that occasion is the power of wisdom.

Insight is the guide; clear comprehension is the goad; wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom, the palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of the investigation of phenomena, a factor of the path, and included within the path.
This, at that time, is the power of wisdom.
What, at that time, is the power of moral shame?
That which, at that time, feels shame where one should feel shame; that which feels shame regarding the undertaking of evil, unwholesome states—this, at that time, is the power of moral shame.
This, at that time, is the power of moral shame (*hiribala*).
What, at that time, is the power of moral dread (*ottappabala*)?
That which, at that time, feels dread where one ought to feel dread, feeling dread regarding the undertaking of evil, unwholesome states.
This, at that time, is the power of moral dread.
What, at that time, is non-greed?

That which at that time is non-greed, non-covetousness, the state of being non-covetous, absence of lust, absence of lusting, the state of being free from lust, lack of longing, and the wholesome root of non-greed.
At that time, this is non-greed.
What at that time is non-hatred?
That which at that time is non-hatred, the state of being without hatred, the quality of being without hatred, non-ill will, non-malice, and the root of wholesomeness that is non-hatred.
At that time, this is non-hatred.
What at that time is non-delusion?
It is the wisdom at that time, which is understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, and close examination.
Discernment, wisdom, skill, sagacity, discrimination, reflection, investigation, breadth, intelligence, guidance, insight, clear comprehension,
the goad, understanding, the faculty of understanding, the power of understanding, the sword of understanding, the palace of understanding, the light of understanding,
the radiance of understanding, the lamp of understanding, the jewel of understanding, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena, and right view.
The investigation-of-states enlightenment factor, which is a path factor included in the path—
this, at that time, is non-delusion.
What, at that time, is non-covetousness?

Whatever at that time is non-greed, non-covetousness, the state of being uncovetous, lack of lust, lack of lusting, the state of being without lust, non-covetousness, and the wholesome root of non-greed— this, at that time, is non-covetousness.
What, at that time, is non-ill-will?
Whatever at that time is non-hatred, non-hating, the state of being without hate, non-malice, non-ill-will, the wholesome root of non-hatred—
this, at that time, is non-malice.
What, at that time, is right view?
Whatever at that time is wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, close discernment, precise discernment, sagacity, skill,
subtlety, discrimination, reflection, examination, breadth, intelligence, guidance, insight,
clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom;
The palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom; non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view,
the factor of enlightenment consisting of investigation of phenomena, a factor of the path, included within the path—
this, at that time, is right view.
What on that occasion is moral shame (*hirī*)?
That which on that occasion is a sense of shame, a feeling of shame where there should be shame, a feeling of shame regarding the undertaking of evil and unwholesome states—
this on that occasion is moral shame.
What on that occasion is moral dread (ottappa)?
That which on that occasion is moral dread, the state of being morally afraid, the being morally afraid of the undertaking of evil, unwholesome states—
this on that occasion is moral dread.
What at that time is bodily tranquility?

That which at that time is the tranquility, the subsiding, the calming, the complete calming, and the state of being completely calmed of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—the factor of enlightenment that is tranquility:
this at that time is bodily tranquility.
What on that occasion is serenity of mind?
That which on that occasion is the serenity, the extreme serenity, the tranquillizing, the extreme tranquillizing, the state of having been tranquillized, of the consciousness-aggregate;
this is the enlightenment factor of serenity, and it is on that occasion the serenity of mind.
What on that occasion is buoyancy of the body?
That which on that occasion is buoyancy, buoyant transformation, non-sluggishness, and non-distension of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this on that occasion is buoyancy of the body.
What on that occasion is buoyancy of mind?
That which on that occasion is buoyancy of the consciousness-aggregate, buoyancy in its transformation, absence of sluggishness, absence of rigidity—
this on that occasion is buoyancy of mind.
What at that time is bodily plasticity?
That which at that time is the plasticity, malleability, non-hardness, and non-rigidity of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this at that time is bodily plasticity.
What on that occasion is plasticity of consciousness?
That which on that occasion is plasticity, malleability, absence of rigidity, absence of stiffness, in the aggregate of consciousness—
this on that occasion is plasticity of consciousness.
What at that time is bodily wieldiness?
That which at that time is the wieldiness, the state of wieldiness, the condition of wieldiness of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
at that time, this is bodily wieldiness.
What on that occasion is wieldiness of mind?
That which on that occasion is the wieldiness, the state of being wieldy, the wieldiness of the consciousness aggregate—
this on that occasion is the wieldiness of mind.
What at that time is bodily proficiency? That which at that time is the proficiency,
the state of proficiency, the condition of proficiency of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this at that time is bodily proficiency.
What on that occasion is proficiency of consciousness?
That which on that occasion is the proficiency, the state of proficiency, the condition of proficiency of the aggregate of consciousness—
this on that occasion is proficiency of consciousness.
What at that time is bodily rectitude? That which at that time is the straightness,
rectitude, lack of crookedness, lack of curvature, and lack of deviousness of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, and the aggregate of mental formations—
this at that time is bodily rectitude.
What at that time is rectitude of mind? That which at that time is the straightness,
rectitude, absence of crookedness, absence of curvature, and absence of deviousness of the aggregate of consciousness—
this at that time is rectitude of mind.
What is mindfulness at that time? That which at that time is mindfulness,

constant mindfulness, specific mindfulness, mindfulness, the state of being mindful, the state of bearing in mind, the state of not losing, the state of not forgetting, mindfulness, the faculty of mindfulness, the power of mindfulness, right mindfulness, the factor of enlightenment that is mindfulness, the path-factor, and that which is included within the path—
this is the mindfulness that exists at that time.
What on that occasion is clear comprehension (*sampajañña*)?
It is the wisdom (*paññā*) on that occasion which is understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena (*dhammavicaya*), discernment, close discernment,
precise discernment, sagacity, skill, subtlety, discrimination, reflection, examination, breadth, and intelligence.

Insight is the guide; clear comprehension is the goad; wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom, the palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom, non-delusion, the investigation of phenomena, right view, the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment, a factor of the path, and included within the path.
This, at that time, is clear comprehension.
What, at that time, is serenity?
It is the stability, steadiness, steadfastness, non-wavering, non-distraction, and state of mental non-distraction of the mind at that time.
Tranquility— the faculty of concentration, the power of concentration, right concentration, the concentration factor of enlightenment, the path factor, and that which is included in the path—
is at that time what constitutes tranquility.
What, at that time, is insight?
Whatever at that time is wisdom, understanding, investigation, thorough investigation, investigation of phenomena, discernment, close discernment, precise discernment, sagacity, skill,
subtlety, discrimination, reflection, examination, breadth, intelligence, guidance, insight,
clear comprehension, the goad, wisdom, the faculty of wisdom, the power of wisdom, the sword of wisdom; this is called the faculty of wisdom.
The palace of wisdom, the light of wisdom, the radiance of wisdom, the lamp of wisdom, the jewel of wisdom; non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view,
the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a factor of the path, included within the path— at that time,
this is what constitutes insight.
What on that occasion is exertion (*paggāha*)?

It is the arousal of mental energy (*vīriyārambha*), the striving, the endeavor, the perseverance, the effort, the enthusiasm, the fortitude, the steadfastness, the firmness, the unfaltering exertion, the non-abandonment of zeal, the non-laying-down of the burden, and the uplifting of the burden that there is on that occasion.
Energy, the faculty of energy, the power of energy, right effort, the factor of enlightenment that is energy, the path-factor included in the path—
this, at that time, is exertion (*paggāha*).
What, at that time, is non-distraction (*avikkhepa*)?
At that time, whatever stability, steadfastness, firmness, non-distraction, non-confusion, state of mental non-confusion, serenity, the faculty of concentration,
the power of concentration, right concentration, the concentration factor of enlightenment, the path factor,
and that which is included in the path there is— this, at that time, is non-confusion.
Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time—
these phenomena are wholesome.
At that time, there are four aggregates, two bases, and two elements.
There are three nutriments; there are nine faculties; there is five-factored jhāna; there is the eightfold path;
there are seven powers; there are three roots; there is one contact; there is one feeling;
there is one perception; there is one volition; there is one consciousness; there is one aggregate of feeling; there is one aggregate of perception.
there is one aggregate of formations, one aggregate of consciousness, one mind base, one mind faculty,
one mind-consciousness element, one mental object base, one mental-object element;
or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time.
These states are wholesome … [as before] … What, at that time, is the aggregate of formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)? Contact, volition, applied thought,
sustained thought, rapture, one-pointedness of mind, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, [the faculty of concentration, and the faculty of wisdom].
The faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the life-faculty, the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," right view,
right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration,
the power of faith, the power of energy, the power of mindfulness, the power of concentration, the power of wisdom, the power of moral shame, the power of moral dread, non-greed, and non-hatred.
Non-delusion, non-covetousness, non-ill will, right view, moral shame, moral dread, serenity of body, serenity of mind, lightness of body,
lightness of mind, malleability of body, malleability of mind, wieldiness of body, wieldiness of mind, proficiency of body,
proficiency of mind, rectitude of body, rectitude of mind, mindfulness, clear comprehension, tranquility, insight, exertion, and non-distraction.

Or whatever other dependent-originated, immaterial phenomena exist at that time, excluding the aggregate of feeling, excluding the aggregate of perception, and excluding the aggregate of consciousness— this, at that time,
is the aggregate of mental formations (*saṅkhārakkhandha*).
…pe… These phenomena are wholesome (*kusala*).
What states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops supramundane jhāna that leads to liberation, conduces to the waning of existence,
and results in the abandoning of wrong views for the attainment of the first stage— secluded from sensual pleasures, and so forth— one enters and dwells in the first jhāna.
The practice is painful and progress is slow; at that time there is contact … pe … there is non-distraction … pe … these states are wholesome.
What states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops supramundane jhāna that leads to liberation and results in the dismantling of attachments—
for the sake of abandoning views and for the attainment of the first stage— being quite secluded from sensual pleasures … [as before] … one enters and dwells in the first jhāna,
which is difficult to practice and quick in direct knowledge; at that time there is contact … [as before] … there is non-distraction … [as before].
These states are wholesome.
Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops supramundane jhāna that is emancipating, leading to the destruction [of clinging], for the abandoning of views—
For the attainment of the first stage, quite secluded from sensual desires … [as above] … he enters and dwells in the first jhāna,
which is of easy progress and sluggish direct knowledge; at that time there is contact … [as above] … there is non-distraction … these states are wholesome.
Which states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops supramundane jhāna that is leading to liberation, tending toward the diminution [of defilements],
for the abandoning of wrong views and for the attainment of the first stage— secluded from sensual pleasures, etc.— one enters and dwells in the first jhāna.
At that time there is pleasant practice with quick direct knowledge; there is contact … pe … there is non-distraction … pe … these states are wholesome.
What states are wholesome?

At whatever time one develops supramundane jhāna that is leading to liberation and conducive to the waning of existence, for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first stage: with the subsiding of applied and sustained thought, ... [as before] ...
the second jhāna ... the third jhāna ...
the fourth jhāna ... [as before].
He enters and dwells in the first jhāna …pe… the fifth jhāna, which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge …pe… [or] which is difficult to practice but quick in direct knowledge …pe….

The path of easy progress with sluggish direct knowledge …pe… the path of easy progress with swift direct knowledge: at that time there is contact …pe… there is non-distraction …pe… these states are wholesome.
The Path of Purification. 2.1.5.2.
Emptiness.
What states are wholesome?
At whatever time one develops supramundane jhāna that is leading to liberation, conducive to the waning of existence,
for the abandoning of views and for the attainment of the first stage— being quite secluded from sensual pleasures … [as above] … one enters and dwells in the first jhāna,
which is void; at that time there is contact … [as above] … there is non-distraction … [as above].
These states are wholesome.
Which states are wholesome?

At whatever time one develops supramundane jhāna that leads to liberation, conduces to the waning of existence, and is for the abandoning of wrong views and the attainment of the first stage—where, with the subsiding of applied and sustained thought, one enters and dwells in the second jhāna... [and so forth].
the third jhāna …pe… the fourth jhāna …pe… the first jhāna …pe…
One enters and dwells in the fifth jhāna, which is emptiness; at that time there is contact … pe … there is non-distraction … pe … these states are wholesome.
Emptiness.
2.1.5.3. The Practice Based on Emptiness (Suññatāmūlakapaṭipadā) Which states are wholesome?

For the attainment of the first stage, quite secluded from sensual pleasures … [as above] … he enters and dwells in the first jhāna,
